issues.t: Oil sludge or coolant in the oil ruins the engine (2.7L)
issues.sym: Knocking or ticking that gets worse, an oil pressure light, milky or very dark thick oil, coolant that keeps going down with no outside leak, and eventually an engine that seizes or won't restart.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 runs hot and holds little oil, so it is prone to sludge, especially when oil changes are stretched. Its water pump sits behind the timing chain, and when the pump's seal or gasket leaks, coolant goes straight into the oil and destroys the bearings.
issues.next: Change the oil on time with the correct synthetic and watch the coolant level closely. If coolant drops with no visible leak or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the water pump checked right away. If the engine is already knocking, get a second opinion before paying for repairs, since replacement is often the realistic fix.

issues.t: Dropped valve seat destroys a cylinder (HEMI)
issues.sym: A sudden misfire with a flashing check engine light, a loud metallic knock, loss of power, smoke from the exhaust, and in some cases the engine dying while you drive. The starter may spin unusually fast because a cylinder has lost compression.
issues.why: The 5.7L HEMI uses valve seats pressed into its aluminum heads. If the head runs hot, often after a cooling problem, a seat can loosen and fall into the cylinder, smashing the valve, piston and cylinder wall.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if it starts knocking hard; driving on it spreads the damage. Have a compression test done. Expect a cylinder head and possibly engine replacement, so get a written quote and compare a remanufactured engine with a repair.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Whining from the transmission, then slipping, no reverse, or the car suddenly losing all drive and refusing to move, sometimes on the highway. Failures are reported anywhere from about 30,000 to over 180,000 miles.
issues.why: The automatic transmissions in these cars wear out internally. Some owners also traced damage to coolant getting into the fluid through the transmission cooler in the radiator, or to failed speed sensors and control modules.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid; if it is pink and milky, coolant has mixed in and the radiator must be replaced along with the transmission repair. Have the codes read before agreeing to a rebuild, since a sensor can cause similar symptoms.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park
issues.sym: The engine starts but the gear lever will not come out of Park even with your foot on the brake. It may free up after a few tries or not at all, leaving you stranded.
issues.why: A small pink plastic piece and its spring inside the shift-lock mechanism of the shifter break or come loose, so the lock never releases.
issues.next: Pry off the trim beside the shifter and press the shift-lock release tab to get the car into gear in an emergency. For a lasting fix, have the shifter's shift-lock parts or the whole shifter assembly replaced, and check that the brake lights work, since the brake switch also controls the lock.

issues.t: Engine stalls or cuts out while driving
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off in traffic, at a stop or even at highway speed, and steering becomes heavy. It may restart right away or only after sitting.
issues.why: Owners and shops have traced it to failing crankshaft or camshaft position sensors, a faulty engine computer (PCM), or the fuel tank venting problem described separately. Often no single cause is confirmed.
issues.next: Have the codes read as soon as possible after a stall, even if no light is on. Sensor replacement is common and is often tried first. Because stalling is a safety risk, avoid busy highways until it is found.

issues.t: Stalls after filling the gas tank
issues.sym: Shortly after refueling the engine stalls at a stop or while driving, or it takes a lot of cranking to start. The gas pump may also click off early.
issues.why: Liquid fuel gets past the tank's fill and vent valve into the evaporative emissions canister and purge valve. That floods the engine with raw fuel vapor and can saturate the canister.
issues.next: Stop filling at the first click and never top off. Have the evaporative system checked; repairs can include the tank vent valve, canister and purge solenoid, and in some cases the fuel tank.

issues.t: ESP light comes on and the car loses power
issues.sym: The ESP (stability control) light flashes or stays on, sometimes with the ABS light, and the car stops accelerating normally or stalls. Restarting usually brings things back to normal for a while.
issues.why: No single cause has been confirmed. Wheel speed sensor, throttle and electrical module faults have all been blamed, and the car cuts power when the stability system thinks something is wrong.
issues.next: Have the ABS and engine codes read while the lights are on. If it keeps happening, avoid using cruise control and get it diagnosed, since losing power at speed is dangerous.

issues.t: Clunking front suspension and fast tie rod wear
issues.sym: Clunks or thumps over bumps and road seams, a loose or wandering feel in the steering, and uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front tension strut bushings, ball joints, control arm bushings, tie rods and sway bar links on these heavy cars wear out early. Owners often replace several parts before finding the worn one.
issues.next: Have the whole front end inspected at once so the right part is found, then get an alignment. Worn tie rods and ball joints affect steering, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts (HEMI)
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the engine that is loudest on a cold start and fades as it warms up, sometimes with an exhaust smell.
issues.why: Heat makes the HEMI's cast iron exhaust manifolds warp, which snaps the bolts, usually at the rear of the passenger side, and lets exhaust leak out.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm where the tick comes from, since it can sound like a lifter problem. Replacing the broken bolts and gasket fixes it; extracting snapped bolts adds labor.

issues.t: Gauges drop to zero while driving
issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer and other gauges suddenly fall to zero and warning lights flicker, then come back.
issues.why: Communication faults in the front control module (FCM) and integrated power module, or in the instrument cluster, interrupt the signal to the gauges.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have a shop scan all modules for stored communication codes. Software updates and module replacement are the usual fixes.

issues.t: Power module (TIPM) failure causes odd electrical faults
issues.sym: Hard starting or cranking with no start, the fuel pump running when it should not, stalling, the horn going off on its own, or wipers and windows acting up.
issues.why: The totally integrated power module (TIPM) under the hood controls power to many systems. When its internal relays or circuits fail, several unrelated things go wrong at once.
issues.next: Have a shop that knows Chrysler products test the TIPM before replacing the fuel pump or other parts. A new or rebuilt module is the usual fix.

issues.t: Headlights and other lights flicker or cut out
issues.sym: The headlights, parking lights and dash lights flicker or go out while driving even though the switch is on. Turning the switch off and on can bring them back.
issues.why: Owners suspect the headlight switch or a relay or module that controls the lights, but no single cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: Treat this as urgent, since losing headlights at night is dangerous. Have the headlight switch and lighting circuit tested.

issues.t: Rear power windows stop working
issues.sym: One or both rear windows stop going up or down. It can be on and off, and sometimes pressing the switch several times or tapping the door panel makes it work again.
issues.why: A worn window motor is the most common repair, though a corroded switch, connector or poor ground can do the same thing.
issues.next: Have the motor tested at the door connector. If power reaches the motor and it does not run, replace the motor; if not, check the switch and wiring.

issues.t: Key breaks inside and won't start the car
issues.sym: The key turns but the car will not start or the key feels loose, and the spare may fail the same way.
issues.why: The plastic key head breaks internally, damaging the chip and buttons that the car needs to recognize the key.
issues.next: Order a new key and have it programmed by a dealer or locksmith. Keep a working spare.

issues.t: Driveshaft rubber coupling fails
issues.sym: A vibration, clunk or thumping from under the middle of the car when pulling away or shifting.
issues.why: The rubber coupling (flex disc) that joins the driveshaft to the transmission or axle cracks and breaks down with age and miles.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft couplings inspected. Replace a cracked one before it lets go, because a loose driveshaft can damage the car.

issues.t: Takata air bag inflators can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The driver and passenger front air bags can explode with too much force in a crash and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: The Takata inflators break down after years of heat and humidity. Recalls 15V313 (driver) and 16V352 (passenger) cover these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the free replacement done right away if it is still open.

issues.t: Car may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park, but the car can roll because the park pawl does not lock the transmission.
issues.why: A plug that holds the park pawl's anchor shaft may have been installed wrong, letting the shaft move. Recall 05V460 adds a retaining bracket.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake, and have the free recall repair done if it is open.

issues.t: Loose battery cable can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Possible burning smell, flickering electrical power or a no-start, though there may be no warning before a fire.
issues.why: The battery cable nut at the firewall stud may not have been tightened, and the loose connection can overheat behind the dashboard. Recall 04V334 covers it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done. Stop driving and get the car checked if you smell burning plastic.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchors may lack welds (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving.
issues.why: Some cars left the factory missing spot welds on a rear floor reinforcement, so the rear seat belt and child seat anchors could tear loose in a crash. Recall 04V333 covers it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it inspected and repaired free, especially if you carry children in the back.

issues.t: Front shoulder belt bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually none, though a loose upper seat belt mount may rattle or move.
issues.why: The bolts holding the front shoulder belt height adjusters may not have been tightened, so the belt could come free in a crash. Recall 04V335 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check and tighten the bolts for free under the recall.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can wear through (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near the engine, a soft or sinking brake pedal, or the brake warning light.
issues.why: On 2.7L cars a rear brake tube can rub against the EGR tube until it wears a hole. Recall 06V149 replaces the tubes and adds a clip.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft, do not drive the car. Check your VIN for this recall and get it fixed free.

issues.t: Gearshift cable can come off (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows one gear while the transmission is in another, and the car could move when you expect it to stay put.
issues.why: The gearshift cable can pop out of its bracket on the transmission. Recall 08V583 adds a locking clip.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park and have the free recall repair done.

issues.t: Drive wheels can briefly lock during shifts (recall)
issues.sym: If you shift to Neutral and back to Drive above about 40 mph, the rear wheels can lock for a moment.
issues.why: A software fault in the powertrain computer caused it. Recall 06V341 reprograms the computer.
issues.next: Do not shift into Neutral at speed, and have the free software update done if it is still open.

issues.t: ABS software can lock the rear brakes (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock up during some hard or uneven braking, making the car slide or spin.
issues.why: A software error in the anti-lock brake module allowed rear-wheel lockup. Recall 06V493 reprograms it.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the free ABS update done before driving in slippery weather.

issues.t: Rear axle hub nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a rear wheel, then loss of drive if the axle shaft comes out.
issues.why: The rear hub nuts were not crimped at the factory, so they could back off and let the half-shaft separate. Recall 08V295 covers it.
issues.next: Have the free recall check done. If you hear clunking from the rear, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Key can stick between Start and On and stall (recall)
issues.sym: After starting, the key may not spring all the way back to On. The engine can then shut off while driving, cutting power steering, power brakes and the air bags.
issues.why: Parts of the ignition switch can hold the key between positions. Recall 14V567 fixes the switch.
issues.next: Make sure the key returns fully to On after starting, and have the free recall repair done.
